contests.title: Proposition 428: Sahuarita Unified School District 15% Maintenance and Operation Budget Override
contests.scopeNote: Voters of Sahuarita Unified School District No. 30.

measures.questionText:
Shall the Governing Board of Sahuarita Unified School District No. 30 of Pima County, Arizona (the
“District”), adopt a General Maintenance and Operation Budget that includes an amount that exceeds
the revenue control limit specified by statute by 15% for fiscal year 2027/2028 and for six (6) subsequent
years as described below? The fiscal year 2027/2028 budget override authority represents an extension
and increase of the existing budget override authority which is scheduled to phase down by one-third
for fiscal year 2028/2029, by another one-third for fiscal year 2029/2030, and will terminate for fiscal
year 2030/2031 if the voters do not approve the override.

The amount of the proposed increase of the proposed budget over the alternate budget for fiscal year
2027/2028 is estimated to be $427,959. In fiscal years 2027/2028 through 2031/2032 the amount of the
proposed increase will be 15% of the District’s revenue control limit in each of such years, as provided in
Section 15-481(P) of the Arizona Revised Statutes. In fiscal years 2032/2033 and 2033/2034, the amount
of the proposed increase will be 10% and 5%, respectively, of the District’s revenue control limit in each
of such years, as provided in Section 15-481(P) of the Arizona Revised Statutes.

Any budget increase authorized by this election shall be entirely funded by a levy of taxes
on the taxable property in this school district for the year for which adopted and for six
(6) subsequent years, shall not be realized from monies furnished by the state and shall
not be subject to the limitation on taxes specified in Article IX, Section 18, Constitution
of Arizona. Based on the current net assessed valuation used for secondary property tax
purposes, to fund the proposed increase in the school district’s budget would require
an estimated tax rate of $1.31 per one hundred dollars of assessed valuation used for
secondary property tax purposes and is in addition to the school district’s tax rate that
will be levied to fund the school district’s revenue control limit allowed by law.

voterGuide.summary:
SAHUARITA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 30
NOVEMBER 3, 2026

15% MAINTENANCE AND OPERATION BUDGET OVERRIDE INFORMATION
A STATEMENT AS TO WHY THE 15% MAINTENANCE AND OPERATION
BUDGET OVERRIDE ELECTION HAS BEEN CALLED

The Governing Board of the District has called a special budget override election to be
held on November 3, 2026 to request voter authorization to exceed the Maintenance
and Operation Budget Limit by 15% of the revenue control limit to fund existing
programs, such budget override to be in effect for a period of seven (7) years. The
override authorized by this election shall be funded from a levy of taxes on the taxable
property within the District. The proposed override is a continuation and increase of
the existing 14% override.
With voter approval to continue the override, it is estimated that the total amount
of the 15% override for fiscal year 2027/2028 will be $6,419,388. If the override is not
approved, the existing 14% override will phase out by reducing by one-third ($1,997,143)
in 2028/2029 and another one-third in fiscal year 2029/2030. The estimated secondary
tax rate needed to fund the full override is $1.31 per one hundred dollars of net
assessed valuation for secondary tax purposes. The estimated secondary tax rate for
the proposed override is approximately equal to the existing secondary tax rate for the
current override, as this override will maintain and enhance programs that have been
in place with prior year’s override approvals.
The estimated continuation and increase cost to an owner of a home with a limited
property value of $210,790 (the average value of a home in the District) would be
approximately $277 per year.
The 15% Maintenance and Operation budget override would continue and enhance
funding for programs currently serving District students. This override supports the
District’s efforts to help maintain present levels of service:
•    Fine Arts (Choral, Band, Orchestra, Drama, Dance)
•    Physical Education
•    Instructional Support Staff
•    Safety and Security Campus Monitor Staff
•    Career and Technical Education (CTE)
•    Athletic Programs
•    NJROTC Leadership Program
•    School Counselors
•    Class Size Reduction
•    Program Sponsors
•    Facility Operations Maintenance

Purposes:



(1) The 15% maintenance and operation override authorization is a continuation and increase of the existing 14%
maintenance and operation override authorized by the voters on 11/8/2022. If the override is not approved, the
existing 14% maintenance and operation override will phase out by reducing one-third in fiscal year 2028/2029
and another one-third in fiscal year 2029/2030. The proposed and alternate 2027/2028 budgets represent the
District’s best estimate based on various assumptions relating to student growth and other factors affecting
revenues and expenditures. In adopting such alternate budget, the Governing Board shall follow the procedures
prescribed in A.R.S. Section 15-905 for adopting a budget that does not include any proposed increases not
approved at an election, except for increases levied to meet a desegregation order, if applicable.

voterGuide.passageThreshold: A. If a proposed budget of a school district exceeds the aggregate budget limit for the budget year, at least ninety days before the proposed election the governing board shall order an override election to be held on the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November as prescribed by section 16-204, subsection F for the purpose of presenting the proposed budget to the qualified electors of the school district who by a majority of those voting either shall affirm or reject the budget.
argumentsFor:
This ballot measure is not a new tax. It is a continuation of a local contribution to our schools
that goes back to the 1980s. These dollars are targeted to support educational programs that are
part of a high quality education. They include K-12 programs in music, physical education, and
counseling. This local investment supports middle and high school athletic programs, Career
and Technical Education (CTE) programs, maintenance personnel, and security support staff.
This override funds over 100 jobs of highly skilled professionals who provide services to our
students. Our students continue to be state and nationally recognized for achievement in
many of these programs. These programs have opened doors for college success, workforce
opportunities, and beyond. Without these local dollars, these programs would not exist or
be largely diminished. These targeted investments elevate the opportunities for students,
the total value of our homes, and community prosperity. Great schools are an investment in
education, economic development, workforce investment and quality of life. It is a “win-win”
proposition for all. We ask for your continuation of this investment, without adding a new tax
or any anticipated increase in the current school tax rate.
Governing Board Sahuarita Unified School District No. 30

My wife Lynn and I chose Sahuarita in 2003, our final stop after 42 years of combined military
service. We chose this community and the quality of its schools was a significant part of why.
I was elected to the SUSD Governing Board in 2004, serving 14 years, including two terms as
president. I know firsthand what this district delivers and what sustained investment makes
possible. Now, as Mayor, I watch Sahuarita grow and know that growth is inseparable from the
strength of our schools. Strong schools are the backbone of a strong town!
This isn’t a new tax - it’s a continuation of a funding source that has been in place for years.
Proposition 428 protects more than 100 staff positions and $6.3 million in annual programs:
Fine Arts, Athletics, CTE, NJROTC, Counselors, and smaller class sizes that define SUSD.
Through Sahuarita’s growth and responsible financial stewardship, the total school tax rate is
expected to remain the same and voters can say YES without paying more.
Vote YES on Proposition 428 to renew the funding that already keeps more than 100 positions
and the programs that serve our wonderful 6,000+ students in our school district.
Thomas Murphy
Mayor of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ

Yes for Sahuarita Schools urges the community to support Proposition 428.
Without this override, Sahuarita Unified stands to lose more than 100 staff positions, including
teachers, counselors, coaches, and instructional aides who directly support more than 6,000
students. Class sizes would grow, and programs in fine arts, athletics, NJROTC, and career and
technical education would be reduced or eliminated.
Proposition 428 is not a new tax. It continues the district’s existing tax rate, with no increase
to homeowners. As Sahuarita’s population and tax base continue to grow, that same rate
generates more total revenue for our schools, allowing the district to sustain these programs
without asking any individual homeowner to pay more.
The cost of inaction is real. Communities with strong, well-supported schools see lower crime

rates, higher property values, and a more skilled local workforce, benefits that extend to every
resident, whether or not they have children in the district. Losing this override would put those
benefits at risk for everyone in Sahuarita.
Sahuarita has a long history of standing behind its schools. We urge voters to continue that
support and protect what our community has built by voting YES on Proposition 428.
Fredrick Lewis
Treasurer, Yes for Sahuarita Schools
Tucson, AZ

Great schools make great communities. It really is that simple.
Rancho Sahuarita was built on the belief that when a safe, engaging community is home to
great schools, other key pieces fall into place: strong home values, economic investment,
and the kind of growth that makes a town worth living in. Sahuarita Unified School District is
central to that.
Proposition 428 continues the Maintenance and Operations Override that funds more than 100
staff positions, including teachers, counselors, athletics, fine arts, NJROTC, and instructional
aides. These roles serve more than 6,000 students across our district.
This is not a new tax. Proposition 428 continues the district’s existing tax rate, with no increase
to homeowners. It simply allows Sahuarita Unified to keep the programs and people already in
place, without asking families to pay more.
As our community continues to grow, our schools remain one of the most important
investments we can make together. A YES vote protects the programs and staff our students
depend on, and protects the quality of life that make Sahuarita a place families choose to call
home.
Vote YES on Proposition 428, and keep our community great!
Jeremy Sharpe
Managing Partner, Rancho Sahuarita
Tucson, AZ

Dear Community Members,
The Kiwanis Club of Sahuarita supports the Sahuarita Unified School District Proposition 428
and encourages you to vote YES for the children. This measure helps maintain the strong
educational foundation our students rely on by sustaining classroom resources, supporting
teachers, and protecting essential academic and extracurricular programs.
Proposition 428 is not about adding something new - it’s about preserving what already works.
Our district has consistently focused on student success, safety, and opportunity. Renewing
this funding ensures students continue to benefit from quality instruction, arts and music
programs, career and technical pathways, and the individualized support that helps them
thrive.
A vote for Proposition 428 is a vote for stable, reliable investment in our children and our
community’s future.
Thank you for considering this important measure.
Sincerely,
The Kiwanis Club of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ

Why is voting, “Yes,” on Prop. 428 vitally important?
As a retired educator from the Sahuarita Unified School District, I have witnessed first-hand
the importance of extending the Maintenance and Operational Budget. What did this mean

for me and my former students?
•   Class sizes did not increase, meaning more time for individual instruction.
•   School Counselors retained their crucial jobs, collaborating with teachers to identify
and address students’ individual needs. Instructional Aides provided additional sets
of hands, ears, and eyes to ensure each student is grasping skill-level concepts and
appropriately navigating informational technology.
• Security Staff and Monitors ensured that students were supervised and were learning in
a safe, respectful environment that supported students’ instructional focus.
• Electives, vital to a well-rounded education, continued. Seeing students discover their
passion for the arts—visual, performing, or fine art—is magical; a metamorphosis occurs.
• Sports, NJROTC, and CTE were supported. SUSD#30 has a proud history of scholar-
athletes who pursued professional sports careers. NJROTC gives interested students a
career path, while the CTE programs give internships and jobs.
Let us continue these praiseworthy achievements. Vote Yes on Prop 428.
Mary A. “Mac” Chernoski
Retired Educator
Sahuarita, AZ

Vote YES for Proposition 428 - M&O Override
As parents, educators, and longtime Sahuarita residents, we are joining together to support the
Sahuarita Unified School District Maintenance and Operations Override.
Between us, we have watched our children grow through SUSD classrooms, athletic fields, and
fine arts programs. We have seen firsthand how smaller class sizes, dedicated counselors, and
caring teachers shape a child’s confidence, and how the individualized support our children
needed was only possible because of positions this override funds.
This override is not a new tax. It simply continues funding our community already relies on,
at the current tax rate, to keep counselors, security staff, coaches, and arts instructors in every
school.
Please join us in voting YES for Proposition 428 to keep more than 100 positions funded and
our 6,000-plus students supported.
Edward Navarrete III
Educator, Father, Resident of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ
Suzanne Burt
Mother and Resident of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ
Claudia Ochoa
Mother and Resident of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ

Yes for Sahuarita Schools - Yes on Proposition 428
My name is Kalaina Vasquez, and I am a proud graduate of Sahuarita High School, Class of
2021.
When I moved from Utah during my Junior year, differences in credit systems left me with far
fewer credits than I needed, putting my on-time graduation in serious doubt. The teachers,
counselors, and administrators at Sahuarita High School, including Principal Kneup, refused
to let that setback define my future. Through after-school tutoring and countless hours of
dedicated support, they helped me close the gap and graduated on time with my class in 2021.
That achievement was possible because Sahuarita Unified School District had the staff,
programs, and resources to meet me where I was and help me catch up. Proposition 428

renews the funding that supports these same positions and programs, the ones that make
individualized support like mine possible for the next student who needs it.
I am proud to be a Sahuarita High School graduate and part of the Sahuarita community. I urge
voters to say YES to Proposition 428 so every student has the same chance I did to succeed.
Kalaina Vasquez
SUSD Alumna and Resident of Sahuarita
Sahuarita, AZ

Proposition 428 - Why It Matters
When I chose to make Sahuarita my home, it was the diversity of homeownership options that
drew me in, a community built for families at every stage of life. That same diversity is what
makes our schools so special.
As a retired medical professional, I spent my career caring for people. Retirement gave me the
chance to build something just as meaningful: relationships with the children and families of
this community. I see their enthusiasm every day, the pride they take in their programs, their
classes, and the teachers who show up for them.
Good schools do not just shape good students. They shape good communities, and they
protect the home values every one of us has invested in.
I am voting YES on Proposition 428, and I ask you to join me.
Myron Baker
Retired Medical Professional and Sahuarita Resident
Sahuarita, AZ

Proposition 428- The Future of Our Children
I chose to make my home in Sahuarita because of the diversity, the strong youth focus, and
the humanitarian spirit of this community.
My grand babies attend Sahuarita Unified schools, and their education matters deeply to me.
I value small classroom sizes because they allow teachers to give each child individualized
focus. In larger classrooms, the brilliance of a child can too easily be missed, and so can the
needs of children requiring special support.
Small classrooms let teachers see every student, including those with special needs, and
support them well. The valued knowledge and experience of our educators is what makes this
possible. In a smaller setting, that expertise goes further, allowing teachers to meet each child’s
needs in a way an overcrowded classroom never could.
Proposition 428 renews the funding that makes this possible. It supports the teachers and
instructional aides who provide the proper learning and guidance that keeps our classrooms
staffed and our kids supported.
I am passionate about this community and about our children’s future. Proposition 428 is a
great foundation for both. Please vote YES on Proposition 428 this November.
Cheryl Thompson
Sahuarita Resident
Sahuarita, AZ
